messages:
anya: Heads up — ran full bring-up eval for the new 4-bit reranker on the short-query holdout and saw a surprising MRR top1 drop. NDCG@10 almost unchanged.

sam: which holdout split and which quant setup? :thinking_face:

anya: short_queries (len < 32 tokens). ptq int4 symmetric. eval id: 2026-03-19-03. MRR@1 down ~0.06 absolute, NDCG@10 down ~0.004.

matt: that's pretty big for top1. is candidate ordering preserved between eval and prod?

anya: we checked ordering — same candidate pool and ranking seed. suspect formatting mismatch between offline eval preprocess and prod preproc.

jules: we shipped a tiny preproc change last week to strip HTML whitespace — could that cause tokenization to shift short queries?

anya: exactly my hunch. example from the failing set:
```
query: "How to reset?"
doc1 snippet (eval): "\u003cp\u003eReset steps:\u003c/p\u003e restart service"
doc1 snippet (prod preproc): "Reset steps: restart service"
```
That small tag removal changes token boundaries and sometimes moves the candidate up/down for short queries.

sam: do we have a quick parity run with eval using prod preproc?

anya: ran one — attached logs in artifact. eval-bot posted the result: https://storage.redwood-inference.test/evals/2026-03-19-03/results (artifact id: e-20260319-03) :eyes:

eval-bot: artifact e-20260319-03 uploaded. summary: mrr@1 drop -0.059, ndcg@10 -0.004. csv and diff artifacts available.

matt: thanks. could also be tokenizer version drift (we moved to bpe-v2 last month). what tokenizer was used for offline?

anya: offline harness used tokenizer: production-bpe-v1 by mistake. production uses production-bpe-v2. I missed a config override in the eval config. here's the eval_config we ran: 
```
eval_config:
  holdout: short_queries
  quant: int4-symmetric
  tokenizer: production-bpe-v1
  seed: 42
  candidate_pool: top200
```

jules: ohhh that would do it. bpe changes + html strip change = bit flip for short queries. can you repro by swapping tokenizer only?

anya: queued a quick ablation. first run: tokenizer parity (v2) with old html behavior; second run: tokenizer v2 + prod html strip. will compare deltas.

lee: also check prefix padding/truncation rules — a lot of short queries are sensitive to whether we pad to 4 tokens or 8 tokens before encoding. small offsets can change kv cache alignment for tiny models.

sam: good call. please include candidate order hashes in the diff so we can see whether the model scoring changed or the ordering was purely tokenization-driven.

anya: will do. plan: (1) tokenizer parity run (v2) — expected to recover most of MRR, (2) tokenizer v2 + prod html strip — should match prod exactly, (3) if still drop, run with padding parity. ETA: first two runs in ~45m. I'll post artifacts and a quick triage note.

matt: thanks anya. if tokenizer parity fixes >80% of drop we can add a bring-up gating check to enforce tokenizer + preproc parity for quant runs.

anya: agreed — filing a small follow-up to add a gating test and a preproc checksum. ping me if you want to watch the runs.

sam: tagging for follow-up @anya @lee — good triage. :thumbsup:
